notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the text: original tower height (NRHP/New England Lighthouses/Lighthouse Friends 72 ft vs Putnam 1917 30 ft, and Putnam's 80 ft in 1865); 1883-85 alterations (NRHP, NE Lighthouses and Lighthouse Friends differ on detail); Dave/David Duncan (USLHS, Lighthouse Friends) vs Reuben Freeman (NE Lighthouses) after Greenleaf; parrot Mickey (macaw) vs Billy; Lighthouse Friends says the Dec 1887 wave shattered the fog-signal building, but the Portland Daily Press of 30 Dec 1887 reports it moved 18 inches and repaired. NRHP OCR is poor: the year of the brick re-raising reads '18^5' and was matched to 1885 by context; mason 'Nichols' prints as 'Michols'. The widely repeated claim that Lafayette dedicated the light in 1791 (Lighthouse Friends, Wikipedia-derived sources) was left out: unsourced and doubtful. Keeper dates from the USLHS roster (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson); 'Elder M. Jordan' and others were not independently confirmed. Roster lines for Cameron/Sterling as first assistant matched from the USLHS list; Hilt's Matinicus Rock service from New England Lighthouses only. 1916 Bulletin: the 'September 1, 1916' issue date comes from New England Lighthouses; the cached text shows printed pp. 230-231. LHB 1900 page is scan page 50 (printed page not confirmed; index lists Portland Head at 42, 45). LHB 1895 volume label: report year ended June 1895, page not determined. Newspaper search for the Dec 1886 wreck narrative found no account in Chronicling America (only the 29 Dec 1886 auction note and a Jan 1887 wages libel). No Life-Saving Service or lighthouse-board text for 1864 Bohemian, 1850s, 1883-85 in local corpus (LHB begins 1891), so those rest on secondary sources. The 1 Jan 1887 breakup and chicken-pie anecdote rest on secondary sources.
